options.name: Aluminium-lithium alloy
options.note: The standard for tanks and shells since the 1990s: light, well understood, easy to weld.

options.name: Stainless steel
options.note: Heavy but cheap, and it keeps its strength when hot and when cryogenic (Starship, Atlas).
pros: Takes heat and cold without complaint

options.name: Carbon-fibre composite
options.note: The lightest option; hand-laid and baked in an autoclave. It cracks instead of bending, and liquid oxygen can attack it.
cons: Brittle: hidden cracks fail without warning

options.name: Titanium
options.note: Strong, light and corrosion-proof; hard to machine, so the bill is high.

options.name: Copper-alloy chamber
options.note: Copper carries heat away from the chamber wall into the cooling channels. The classic choice.

options.name: Inconel chamber
options.note: A nickel superalloy that stays strong at glowing temperatures. Long life, many restarts.

options.name: 3D-printed chamber
options.note: Laser-sintered in one piece with its channels (like Rocket Lab's Rutherford). Light and cheap, but porosity is hard to inspect.
cons: Newer process: a little less reliable

options.name: Aluminium housing
options.note: Machined aluminium box, gold-foil insulation on top.

options.name: Radiation-hardened housing
options.note: Thicker walls and shielded electronics that shrug off solar storms.
